successCriteria.description: knexfile.ts exists at project root and exports a Knex config using client 'pg', reading the connection string from process.env.DATABASE_URL, with migrations directed at a './migrations' directory using the 'ts' extension.

Running knex migrate:latest against a database with DATABASE_URL set creates three tables — leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances — each with all columns specified in PLAN.md Phase 1 (correct types, nullability, and defaults).

Running knex migrate:rollback drops the most recently migrated table (down function executes dropTableIfExists successfully), and the full migration set is reversible by rolling back all three in order.

The leave_policies.leave_type CHECK constraint rejects any INSERT with a value outside 'annual','sick','emergency','unpaid','maternity','paternity', and the leave_requests.status CHECK constraint rejects any value outside 'DRAFT','SUBMITTED','APPROVED','REJECTED','CANCELLED'.

The leave_requests.leave_type_id and leave_balances.leave_type_id foreign keys both reference leave_policies.id, so inserting a row with a non-existent leave_type_id fails with a referential integrity violation.
The leave_balances table enforces a unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_type_id, year), so a second INSERT with the same combination fails with a unique violation.
Each table's UUID primary key defaults automatically via knex.fn.uuid(), so an INSERT that omits the id column succeeds and populates a valid UUID.

The mechanical compile gate (npm run build && npx jest --passWithNoTests) passes unchanged — knexfile.ts and migrations/ at project root do not appear in tsc --noEmit output and do not break the existing build.

constraints: knexfile.ts and all migration files must reside at project root (outside src/), so they are excluded from the tsc --noEmit build gate which only includes the src/ directory.
The knexfile connection must read process.env.DATABASE_URL (the confirmed config key per HARNESS.json adapters.database.configKey), not a hardcoded connection string.

The knexfile production environment block must mirror the SSL logic in src/shared/db/connection.ts — SSL enabled when NODE_ENV === 'production' using DB_SSL_CA, disabled otherwise — so Knex and the runtime pg Pool connect with parity.

No separate leave_types table may be created; leave_type is an inline varchar column with a CHECK constraint on leave_policies, per the prescriptive PLAN which overrides the conceptual architecture model.
leave_requests.leave_type_id and leave_balances.leave_type_id foreign keys must reference leave_policies.id (per PLAN's literal instruction), not a leave_types table.
Every migration file must export both an up and a down function; up uses knex.schema.createTable and down uses knex.schema.dropTableIfExists for the corresponding table.

UUID primary keys must default via knex.fn.uuid() (Knex 3 supports this for the pg client); created_at and updated_at must be timestamptz NOT NULL with a default of knex.fn.now() so inserts that omit them succeed.
CHECK constraints must be applied via raw SQL (knex.raw) attached to the column, since Knex lacks a first-class check-constraint builder.
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, or tokens in knexfile.ts or migrations (HARNESS.json no-hardcoded-secrets rule, severity critical).
Migration files must import Knex types from 'knex' for editor/runtime typing, but must not be type-checked by the build gate; they are executed by Knex via ts-node at runtime.
outOfScope: The seed migration (004_seed_default_policies) is deferred to Phase 9 — this phase only creates the schema (tables 001–003), not seed data.
No employees, audit_logs, or notifications tables are created in this phase — only leave_policies, leave_requests, and leave_balances.
No repository, service, controller, or route code is produced in this phase — those are Phases 2–8. This phase is migrations and knex config only.

No Jest unit tests for migration files are required — jest.config.js testMatch targets **/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js), and migrations live at project root outside that path; verification is via running knex migrate against a database.
No Knex CLI scripts (e.g., package.json "migrate" npm scripts) are added in this phase unless needed to run migrations; the phase deliverables are knexfile.ts and the three migration files only.

entityInvariants.invariant: A leave policy row's leave_type must always be one of the six allowed values ('annual','sick','emergency','unpaid','maternity','paternity') enforced by a database CHECK constraint; the table cannot hold a row with any other leave_type value.

A leave request row's status must always be one of the five lifecycle states ('DRAFT','SUBMITTED','APPROVED','REJECTED','CANCELLED') enforced by a database CHECK constraint, defaulting to 'DRAFT' on insert; the table cannot hold a row with any other status value.
A leave request's leave_type_id must always reference an existing leave_policies.id row (referential integrity via foreign key); a request cannot exist pointing to a non-existent or deleted policy.

For any given (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) combination there is at most one leave_balances row, enforced by a unique constraint; duplicate balance rows for the same employee, leave type, and year are rejected by the database.
A leave balance's leave_type_id must always reference an existing leave_policies.id row (referential integrity via foreign key); a balance cannot exist pointing to a non-existent policy.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires DATABASE_URL env var to be set and resolvable (dotenv loaded in knexfile); no application-level auth — this is a developer/CI tooling operation.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Fails with a clear Knex error if DATABASE_URL is missing or the database is unreachable; each migration runs in its own transaction and a failure rolls back that migration without leaving a partially-created table.

interfaceConstraints.operation: knex migrate:rollback (revert the last batch of migrations)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: Same as migrate:latest — requires DATABASE_URL; developer/CI tooling operation.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: The down function drops the table via dropTableIfExists, so rolling back a migration that was never applied (or whose table was already dropped) does not error; failures surface as Knex errors.

interfaceConstraints.operation: knexfile.ts Knex.Config export (configuration consumed by the Knex CLI)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth; configuration object. Must load dotenv so process.env.DATABASE_URL resolves from a .env file when present.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: If DATABASE_URL is undefined, Knex will fail at connection time with a pg connection error rather than silently using a default.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The knexfile's connection configuration must match the existing pg Pool setup in src/shared/db/connection.ts — same DATABASE_URL env var as the connection string source, and the same conditional SSL logic (SSL enabled in production via DB_SSL_CA, disabled otherwise) so Knex and the application runtime connect to the same database with the same TLS posture.

The knexfile must use client 'pg' and read the connection string from the DATABASE_URL config key, matching the declared adapter in HARNESS.json (adapters.database.type = postgres, adapters.database.configKey = DATABASE_URL).

knexfile.ts and the migrations/ directory must remain outside the tsconfig.json include scope (which is ["src"]) so they are not type-checked by tsc --noEmit; they must not be added to the include array or moved under src/.

The three migration files must create exactly the tables and columns specified in PLAN.md Phase 1 — leave_policies (migration 001), leave_requests (migration 002), leave_balances (migration 003) — with the prescribed column types, nullability, defaults, CHECK constraints, foreign keys, and the unique constraint on leave_balances (employee_id, leave_type_id, year). The PLAN is prescriptive and overrides the conceptual data model in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (no leave_types table; leave_type_id FK targets leave_policies.id; balances use entitlement_days/used_days/accrued_days/year).

The knexfile and migrations must use the already-installed dependency versions — knex@^3.1.0, pg@^8.7.1, ts-node@^10 — without adding new runtime dependencies; no @types/knex is needed since Knex 3 ships its own TypeScript types.

integrationPoints.why: The knexfile must connect to the same database the application runtime uses — same DATABASE_URL and SSL configuration — so migrations apply to the database the repositories will query.
The knexfile.ts is the entry point the Knex CLI consumes to locate and run the TypeScript migrations in the ./migrations directory via ts-node.

The leave_policies table created in migration 001 is the target of the seed data migration in Phase 9; the schema must exist before seed inserts run, establishing a forward dependency on this phase's table structure.

The repository layer in Phase 3 will query leave_requests and leave_balances tables whose schema is defined by migrations 002 and 003 in this phase; column names and types must align so repository queries map correctly.
